title: How to choose a vending machine location in Malaysia
excerpt: Use a seven-point site survey to compare footfall, product demand, access, utilities and placement terms before committing to a vending site.
opening: A busy lobby and a good vending site are two different things. A corridor where people hurry to the car park may see more traffic than a break room, while the break room gives staff time to browse and a reason to return. Compare where people stop, what they already buy and when they have few alternatives.
checklist: Count relevant footfall. Use the same observation window at each candidate site. Record arrivals, lunch breaks and shift changes separately.
Test the product fit. Ask regular users what they would buy, when and at what price. Bring photos of three possible products to make the questions concrete.
Map alternatives. Record the opening hours, prices and walking distance of the closest canteen or shop.
Walk the purchase journey. Check visibility from the main route, room to queue and whether customers can use the touchscreen and collect items comfortably.
Walk the delivery route. Measure doorways, turns and lifts. Confirm power, connectivity, ventilation and the supplier’s required clearances.
Check access and security. Identify who can enter, who opens the site for service and how incidents are reported.
Write down the economics. Record rent or commission, utilities, the trial term, notice period and who pays to move the machine.
close: Bring a floor photo, observations by time slot and draft terms to the site review. Treat unknowns such as lift fit or power access as open items before committing.
